title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: when a document is voided or accomplished
content:
## Scope

This Bills of Lading and Transport Documents policy states when a transport document is voided and when it is accomplished, and what may still be recorded against an accomplished document.

## Formal clauses

1. A draft or approved document is voided when its booking is cancelled or when the documentation party withdraws the shipping instructions. No fee is charged for a document that was never issued.
2. A surrendered document is voided only when a switch bill replaces it under the switch bill rules.
3. An issued document is never voided by the desk. Lost originals are replaced within the same document under the lost original reissue rules.
4. A released document is accomplished by the system when delivery is completed. Nothing further may then be recorded against it except payments of fees already booked.

## Status by status

| Status of the document | Can it be voided? | On what ground |
|---|---|---|
| Draft | Yes | booking cancelled, or shipping instructions withdrawn |
| Approved | Yes | booking cancelled, or shipping instructions withdrawn |
| Issued | No, never by the desk | lost originals are handled by a replacement set within the same document |
| Surrendered | Only in one case | a switch bill replaces it |
| Released | No voiding ground is provided | it is accomplished by the system when delivery is completed |

## Points of judgement

- **Hypothetical case:** the documentation party withdraws its shipping instructions while the draft is awaiting approval. The draft is voided, and because the document was never issued, no fee is charged.
- **The customer asks the desk to void an issued document because an original is missing.** The desk does not void an issued document; a lost original is dealt with by a replacement set within the same document.
- **A fee remittance arrives after the document is accomplished.** A payment of a fee already booked may still be recorded; nothing else may.
